text: The authors propose training agents via self-play on a zero-sum debate game in which two agents take turns making short statements about a question or proposed action, after which a human judges which agent gave the most true, useful information. They state that, by analogy to complexity theory, debate with optimal play can answer any question in PSPACE given polynomial-time judges (direct judging answers only NP questions), and report an MNIST experiment in which debate raises a sparse classifier judge's accuracy from 59.4% to 88.9% with 6 pixels and from 48.2% to 85.2% with 4 pixels.
title: AI safety via debate: zero-sum self-play debate game judged by a human
